text:
Alex Chen: Quick sync — planning dedicated pool sizing for Acme.health (EU-WEST). They expect ~200 peak RPS for chat generation, avg ~512 tokens/request, spiky during business hours. Can we agree on a commit level + buffer and any gotchas for billing/quotas?
Priya Nambiar: Do we have their 95/99 percentile traffic shape? 200 rps peak is different if it's sustained vs 10m spikes.
Marco Ruiz: From the intake sheet: 200rps 95th over 15m windows, bursts up to 350rps for ~3m at hour boundaries. Daily baseline ~40rps.
Sandeep Rao: For model pick — they prefer guppy-extended (causal) equivalent. On H100 a single shard can handle ~18k tokens/s (conservative) with our current batching.
Lisa Park: Quick calc:
```
peak_rps = 200
avg_tokens = 512
tokens_per_sec = peak_rps * avg_tokens  # 102400 tokens/s
tokens_per_min = tokens_per_sec * 60     # 6,144,000 tokens/min
```
If H100 handles 18k tokens/s -> 18,000 tokens/s ~= 1,080,000 tokens/min per GPU. So tokens_per_min / 1,080,000 = ~5.7 GPUs.
Alex Chen: So ~6 H100 GPUs to sustain peak 200rps continuous. But they have 3m bursts to 350rps -> that pushes to ~11 GPUs transient if we want no throttling.
Priya Nambiar: For commits we usually size for 95th (15m) with a 20% headroom to avoid frequent overages. So 6 * 1.2 -> 7.2 -> round to 8 GPUs committed. Overage pricing covers the short bursts.
Sandeep Rao: Agree. Also need to factor in maintenance/eviction buffer and cross-region fallbacks are not acceptable for them (health regs). So commit in eu-west only.
Marco Ruiz: Cloud-side: check quota for GPUs in eu-west — last time there was a soft quota of 32 GPUs per project in that region; we may need to request increase if they have other customers. Capacity-bot: GPU quota for eu-west1 currently 48 total, 12 H100 available for allocation to Dedicated.
Alex Chen: Billing nuance: customer contract wants monthly committed v. reserved price with overage at 1.5x list. Does that map cleanly to our Reserved Capacity product?
Lisa Park: Yes — we map committed GPUs to reserved capacity SKU. Need to build an invoice example for legal — show committed 8 GPUs monthly with expected utilization 65% and peak headroom 20%. Include runtime GPU-hours estimate.
Priya Nambiar: Suggested commit = 8 H100-equivalent units in eu-west, 3-month ramp (4/8/8 for first three months) or annual discount. Also recommend a scheduled autoscale burst pool (pay-as-you-go) for the 3m spikes to avoid over-commit.
Sandeep Rao: Ops note: autoscale for Dedicated requires extra control plane capacity; plan ~10% more control-plane vCPU for the region. Also we should pin model version and quantization to avoid perf variance.
Marco Ruiz: Action items:
- @Sandeep: verify end-to-end throughput figure with bench tool and run: `./bench --model guppy-ext --gpu h100 --rps 200 --batching auto`
- @Lisa: draft invoice + sample commit SLA with 8 GPUs and burst pool pricing
- @Priya: confirm ramp schedule with sales & legal and get customer OK on eu-west only constraint
- @Alex: open a quota request if capacity-bot reports < 12 available after other reservations
capacity-bot: Noted. Created ticket #INC-2026 for capacity request; ETA ~48h.
Alex Chen: Sounds good. If we get quota and bench numbers match, I'll propose commit: 8 H100-equivalents (eu-west), 3-month ramp, autoscale burst capacity for spikes. Any objections?
Lisa Park: No objections. Will start invoice draft. :thumbsup:
Priya Nambiar: Fine by me. Keep me looped for contract language.
Sandeep Rao: I'll run bench today and post results here. Expect a few log snippets and a short perf table.
Marco Ruiz: I'll monitor region inventory and flag if another customer schedules a large commit this week.
Alex Chen: Thanks all — will follow up in 24h with bench & quota updates.
